recent_posts.title: Watermill Quickstart
recent_posts.summary: Watermill has released an interactive quickstart tutorial for learning their Go library for building event-driven applications. The hands-on training covers core APIs (Publisher/Subscriber, Router, CQRS), Kafka integration, topic topology, middleware, consumer groups, message ordering, the Outbox pattern with PostgreSQL, and switching Pub/Sub implementations with Redis. The tutorial runs directly in your IDE without requiring Docker setup or browser-based coding.

recent_posts.title: Debugging Go programs with VS Code debugger and logging techniques
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide covering multiple debugging approaches in Go using Visual Studio Code. Demonstrates basic logging with fmt.Println and log.Printf functions, setting up breakpoints in VS Code debugger, using conditional breakpoints, and configuring launch files for debugging programs that require command-line arguments. Shows practical examples of stepping through code execution and inspecting variable values during runtime.

recent_posts.title: Making a game with Pion
recent_posts.summary: Explores building cross-platform multiplayer games using WebRTC datachannels with Pion (a Go WebRTC library) and Ebitengine. Covers the advantages of WebRTC over WebSockets for real-time gaming, discusses various WebRTC implementations, and presents a practical example of peer-to-peer game networking without dedicated servers or port forwarding.

recent_posts.title: DevLink: The Peer-to-Peer Toolkit for Frictionless Development
recent_posts.summary: DevLink is a peer-to-peer CLI toolkit that eliminates staging friction by enabling direct, encrypted connections between developers' local environments. It allows instant sharing of code, databases, Docker images, and services without cloud dependencies, reducing context switching and integration time from 30-60 minutes to 30-120 seconds. The tool features ephemeral staging environments, secure secret sharing, P2P Git repositories, live database access, and localhost streaming capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Go Coding Official Standards and Best Practices
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide covering Go's official coding standards and best practices, including code formatting with gofmt, naming conventions, package design principles, error handling patterns, function design, concurrency guidelines, comment conventions, testing approaches, and performance optimization techniques. The guide emphasizes Go's philosophy of simplicity and provides practical code examples for each topic.

recent_posts.title: From Go code to container image with Depot API
recent_posts.summary: A technical walkthrough demonstrating how to build a specialized container building system using Depot's low-level Go SDK. The guide covers the three-step build flow: registering builds with the API, acquiring ephemeral BuildKit machines, and configuring custom build solutions that transform tar archives into container images. The approach provides enterprise-grade build performance with native ARM64 support and persistent caches without managing BuildKit infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: I Made an Online Game Between Mario 64 and Crash Bandicoot on Real Hardware
recent_posts.summary: A hardware hacker creates cross-platform multiplayer between Super Mario 64 on Nintendo 64 and Crash Bandicoot on PlayStation 1 using real vintage consoles. The project involves desoldering cartridge chips, replacing them with a Raspberry Pi Pico for USB communication, reverse engineering PlayStation 1 memory structures, and hijacking kernel space to enable real-time position synchronization between characters across both games.

recent_posts.title: Building REST API and YAML DSL for LLM workflow management service
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of designing a REST API and Domain Specific Language (DSL) for Flowrun, a service for managing LLM workflows. The design covers CRUD operations for providers, models, tasks, accounts, and flows, along with execution endpoints. The DSL uses YAML configuration files inspired by Terraform and Kubernetes, with a state management system to track resource mappings. Key features include idempotent operations using client-generated IDs, embedded JSON schemas for task parameters, and support for parallel flow execution using graph traversal.

recent_posts.title: We Built It, Then We Freed It: Telemetry Harbor Goes Open Source
recent_posts.summary: Telemetry Harbor announces the open-source release of their complete telemetry ingestion platform. The OSS version includes the same production-ready Go-based API, TimescaleDB storage, Redis queuing, and Grafana integration that powers their cloud service. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it can be deployed with a simple docker compose command and supports all existing SDKs. The company explains their decision to open-source as building trust through transparency while maintaining their managed cloud offering for teams preferring hosted solutions.

recent_posts.title: Preserving Order in Concurrent Go Apps: Three Approaches Compared
recent_posts.summary: Explores three approaches to preserve order in concurrent Go applications while maintaining performance benefits. Compares ReplyTo channels, sync.Cond turn-taking, and permission passing chain patterns through detailed benchmarks. The permission passing approach emerges as the winner, offering good performance with zero allocations and clean abstractions for building reusable concurrent operations.
